part: Operations region x dimension scoreboard AT ARRIVAL: RegionDimensionMatrix as a reader arrives at it (table card, the DEFAULT selection, its panel open in a fixed-height slot)
artboards: 08-operations-list-redesign-2026-09-08 (the REDESIGNED artboard; supersedes 08-operations-list for this component)
source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/screens/08-operations-list-redesign-2026-09-08.png (the operator's redesigned artboard, copied into the repo by lane opsmatrix3 on 2026-09-08; the 2026-09-06 08 is left in place as the record of the design it replaces), plus the operator's written spec quoted verbatim in the notes below. Values neither states are taken from the system sheet (screens/00-system-sheet.png, README.md §0.4) and are marked `[system sheet]` on the row that asserts them.
notes: SPEC RE-POINTED 2026-09-09 (lane opsmatrix5), reversing the 2026-09-08 (lane noexpand) revision for THIS COMPONENT ONLY. The operator's /operations STOP SHIP message of 2026-09-09, item 5, verbatim: "Default state on load: first sourced cell of the first sourced row open." Item 3, verbatim: "Arrow keys move the selection; panel follows; Esc closes." That is the opposite of what he wrote on 2026-09-08, verbatim: "the ops page opend to a sub category not just the main page, infastructure capacity and other items should be closed, no items expanded when first navigtaing to a page". COORDINATOR NOTE C1, 2026-09-09, binding and not this lane's to revisit: what the 2026-09-08 ruling forbade is the RETIRED row-expansion pattern, the thing he was looking at when he wrote it and the thing the 2026-09-09 message orders deleted; the new panel's default selection is explicitly wanted, in writing, in the newer message. So this matrix arrives with the first sourced cell of the first sourced row SELECTED and its panel showing, and NOTHING ELSE anywhere on the site opens itself. The site-wide rule, F42, and the rendering guard's no-default-open leg all stand unchanged for every other route and component; the matrix is their ONE allowed exception and it DECLARES itself with data-open-on-mount naming both dates, rather than being exempted by path.

WHY EVERY RE-POINTED ROW IS AT LEAST AS STRONG. Three targets and four forbids here asserted the CLOSED arrival state: no aria-selected cell, no panel, no fact card, no cell carrying the selection tint, one tab stop, the tab stop is the first cell, the foot legend survives. They now forbid what the operator asked for, so they cannot stand as written. None is weakened into a smaller version of itself: each is replaced by a row asserting the EXACT arrival state he named, which is a strictly narrower claim than the one it replaces. "No cell is aria-selected" (any of 30 cells failing) becomes "exactly ONE cell is aria-selected AND it is ASIA x D3" (29 of 30 cells failing, plus a count). "No panel" becomes "the panel is present, its heading names that cell, and it is DECLARED with data-open-on-mount naming both dates" (three assertions where there was one). "No fact card" becomes the three-card cap plus the remainder link on the arrival state. "No cell carries the tint" becomes "exactly one cell carries the tint AND the 2px inset, measured by computed value", which still catches a build that paints a cell without the aria attribute and now also catches one that sets the attribute without painting. "The tab stop is the first cell" becomes "the tab stop is the SELECTED cell", which pins it to a data-derived position rather than to a constant. The at-rest count rows that survive unchanged (six rows, 40px height, 22 absence cells, sticky column, the header hint, the column sub-lines) were never about the selection and are untouched. The fixture makes the narrower claims hard: D1 and D2 hold no facts on any region and EU and US hold none on any dimension, so the default must skip TWO empty rows and TWO empty columns to land on ASIA x D3. A default of row 0 / column 0, of row 0's first sourced cell, or of a column-first scan fails these rows.

THE OPERATOR'S THREE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, verbatim: "at 1440 the matrix card height is constant regardless of selection; no text column in the card is narrower than 560px; no cell contains a word." Each gets a row and a forbid below, asserting the MECHANISM that makes it true, because this runner renders one state and cannot click. The three-state MEASUREMENT that the criteria themselves demand (coordinator note C3: "measured, not asserted") is .discipline/rendering/smoke/ops-matrix-acceptance-smoke.mjs, wired into the rendering guard, which reports the three card heights, the narrowest text column and every cell's rendered text on every run. MEASURED 2026-09-09: card height 757.25px with nothing selected, 757.25px with a cell selected, 757.25px in compare mode (this mount, 900px card at viewport 1440); 680.25px / 680.25px / 680.25px on the composed page at 1440 (card 1032px). Narrowest text column 835px here, 967px composed, against a 560px floor. Thirty body cells, every one an integer score or an em dash.

THE PROSE'S MEASURE, corrected 2026-09-09. Operator ruling, verbatim: "72ch is the MAX line length of the prose (max-width:72ch on the text block); 560px is the MIN width of the column that holds it. A 967px column with a 72ch text block inside is exactly the spec." The build this row was written against read 72ch as a width for the COLUMN and capped the text block at max(560px, 72ch), which put a floor and a measure on one box and made two constraints on two different boxes look like rivals. They are not: the cap is `max-width: 72ch` on the detail sentence and on the claim, and acceptance criterion B ("no text column in the card is narrower than 560px") is measured on the cell and the panel column, which keep their full width. The expected width is unchanged at 572.609px because `max(560px, 72ch)` and `72ch` resolve to the same value in this face; only the reason the number is that number changed.

WHAT MOVED, AND WHY EVERY MOVED ASSERTION IS AT LEAST AS STRONG WHERE IT LANDED. Fourteen rows measured the SELECTED state and the PANEL: the #DCE7FB tint, the 2px #2563EB inset, the panel's background and top rule, its DOM position below the table, its heading string, its two links, the three-card cap, the remainder line, and the five fact-card values. None is deleted and none is weakened. All fourteen moved verbatim to `operations-matrix-selected.json`, whose mount is the SAME component and the SAME fixture with ONE CLICK on the ASIA x D3 cell performed by the mount itself. They are measured on a cell selected through the real click handler, which is a stricter proof than the one they replace: before, they were measured on a state the component produced for itself, so a broken click path could not have failed them. Now it does.

ONE ROW WAS REPHRASED RATHER THAN MOVED. 'the selected cell is the grid's single TAB STOP' asserted `[tabindex="0"]` count 1. That count still holds and is still asserted here, at rest, where there is no selection at all: it is now the proof of ruling R5 ("the first cell is FOCUSABLE without being SELECTED"), and a second row pins the tab stop to the first row's header. Same count, harder state.

THE FOOT STRIP MOVED IN THE PRODUCT, and this spec follows it. It used to render INSIDE the panel, which was safe only while a default selection guaranteed a panel existed. With no default selection the panel is absent on arrival, so the strip that carries the absence legend, the click affordance and the column-scoping count now sits on the CARD, below the panel slot. RE-POINTED AGAIN 2026-09-09: the arrow-key clause is back to `arrow keys move the selection`, which is both the artboard's own foot text and what the 2026-09-09 message restores ("Arrow keys move the selection; panel follows"). The strip stays on the CARD rather than moving back inside the panel, because the panel slot is now a fixed-height box that scrolls its own content and a legend inside a scroller would scroll out of view.

THE OPERATOR'S SPEC, verbatim, which every row below traces to: 'Matrix rows 40px. Cell = Anton 16 score or em dash. Nothing expands in the table. / Click a cell, it gets selection tint #DCE7FB + 2px #2563EB inset; a panel opens under the table (bg #FAFAF8, 1px top rule): header "Region · Dn Dimension · N sourced facts", links "Compare across regions" and "Open profile", facts as fact cards (headline figure Anton 18 inline with 12.5px quote, source line 10.5px), max 3, then "N more facts on the profile". / Click a row header, same panel in compare mode: one headline card per region, stacked, region label on each. / Arrow keys move the selection; panel follows. Default selection: first sourced cell in the first sourced row. / First column sticky; regions beyond five scroll horizontally inside the card; header hint "18 regions · scroll". Footer legend: "not in primary source". / Rail filters scope columns.'

ALL THREE OF THE OPERATOR'S HEX VALUES ARE ALREADY CANONICAL TOKENS in src/app/theme.css, so the component names tokens and this spec measures the resolved colours: #DCE7FB is `--selection` (interaction states), #2563EB is `--monitor` (the band scale), #FAFAF8 is `--page`. No new token was introduced and no raw hex was written into the component.

THE FIXTURE IS AN ATTACK, not a sample (mounts.mjs `OPSMATRIX_ENTRY`). D1 and D2 hold no facts on any region and EU and US hold no facts on any dimension: the shape of the live corpus, where regulatory_feasibility is structurally empty and 75 of 75 rows are ASIA/UK/UAE. The default selection must therefore skip two empty rows AND two empty columns to land on ASIA x D3, which is what the panel-heading row below asserts by naming the exact string that cell produces. A default of row 0 / column 0, or of row 0's first sourced cell, or of a column-first scan, fails that row. ASIA x D3 carries FOUR facts, so the same at-rest render also proves the three-card cap and the 'N more facts on the profile' remainder line, with no interaction to script.

WHAT THIS SPEC CANNOT MEASURE, stated rather than faked: the audit runner reads computed style and textContent of a single rendered state and cannot click or send keys, so the SELECTION MOVING (arrow keys, click-to-select, compare mode on a row header) is proven in RegionDimensionMatrix.npmtest.mjs against the component's own source, and the selected-state STYLING is measured here on the default selection, which is a real selected cell rendered by the real code path. An `expect` key naming an HTML attribute measures as null and reports a false MATCH, so no row below reads one: `aria-selected` and `tabindex` appear only inside SELECTORS, where they are real CSS attribute matches.

children.name: six dimension rows, D1-D6 (operator ruling 3.3, carried forward from the spec this replaces: nothing expands, so a tbody row IS a dimension row and the old 'do not conflate with the Facts tr' caveat is gone)
row 1 is D1 Regulatory feasibility (order check, ruling 3.3: same order everywhere)
every dimension row carries its D-number prefix: the redesigned artboard draws 'D1 Regulatory feasibility' through 'D6 Operational cost' in the table, not just in the rail
MATRIX ROWS 40px (operator spec, first clause)
CELL = ANTON 16 SCORE (operator spec): the display face at 16px, line-height 1
CELL = ... OR EM DASH: an unsourced cell renders the narrow Absence, which IS the artboard's bare dash carrying its closed-vocabulary reason (22 of this fixture's 30 cells)
the grid is a roving tabindex: exactly ONE tab stop, so every other cell is reachable from it by arrow and the table is one Tab away
the card carries its foot legend BELOW the panel slot: the strip that explains the dashes and names the two affordances sits on the CARD, outside the panel's scroller, so it never scrolls out of view
FIRST COLUMN STICKY with a 1px right divider (operator spec)
the header's Dimension cell is sticky too, so the pinned column has a pinned head
the table scrolls horizontally INSIDE the card (the card clips; the scroller is the inner box), and the box is declared to the guard's overflow detector

HEADER HINT states the cells sourced, the percentage and the region count, and adds `scroll →` only when there is somewhere to scroll to (redesigned artboard head aside: `18 OF 30 CELLS SOURCED · 60% · 18 REGIONS · SCROLL →`). The operator's delete list replaces `click a dimension to open its facts` with `N regions · scroll →`; the artboard keeps the two computed figures in front of it and the artboard wins [system sheet: 10.5px uppercase muted]
region column sub-line is the artboard's one-line 'N/6 sourced' form, one per region column [system sheet: 10px, the smallest step on the type scale]

FOOTER LEGEND carries the dash convention, the click affordance and the arrow-key affordance, all three, in the artboard's own words (redesigned artboard, panel foot, left half). RE-POINTED 2026-09-09 from `arrow keys move between cells`: arrows move the SELECTION again (2026-09-09 item 3), which is what the artboard's foot strip says.
the legend states its reason in the closed absence vocabulary AND shows the glyph it explains: the narrow Absence (which IS the em dash) beside the worded one, the artboard's own pairing
the panel foot's right half names the column scoping (redesigned artboard: 'N of M regions · filters scope columns')
AT ARRIVAL, EXACTLY ONE CELL IS SELECTED (operator 2026-09-09 item 5, verbatim: "Default state on load: first sourced cell of the first sourced row open")

and it is the FIRST SOURCED CELL OF THE FIRST SOURCED ROW. The fixture holds no facts on D1, none on D2, and none on EU or US, so only a rows-outer/regions-inner scan that skips two empty rows and two empty columns lands on ASIA x D3; row 0, column 0, or a column-first scan all fail this row

SELECTED CELL FILL #DCE7FB (`--selection`) and a 2px #2563EB (`--monitor`) INSET, measured by computed value on the arrival selection. Inset rather than a border, so a selected cell is still 40px tall

THE ARRIVAL STATE IS DECLARED, not hidden: the panel carries `data-open-on-mount`, the escape hatch open-state-sweep.mjs provides for a ruled-open default, and the declaration text names BOTH operator messages

EXACTLY TWO declared open elements, and both belong to this matrix: the panel and the cell whose tint reports aria-selected. Two rather than one because the sweep allows an element only if it or an ancestor carries the declaration, and the tinted cell is not inside the panel. One exception, one component, not a category, and this count is what keeps the site-wide rule from leaking.

THE PANEL opens UNDER the table, on the `--page` ground #FAFAF8 with a 1px rgba(0,0,0,.12) top rule (operator 2026-09-09, verbatim: "the panel's #FAFAF8 ground and 1px rgba(0,0,0,.12) top rule"). CORRECTED 2026-09-09: the build before this used `--line-2`, rgba(0,0,0,.08), which is not the value he states; the .12 token is `--line-1`

ACCEPTANCE A, THE MECHANISM: the panel is a FIXED-HEIGHT SLOT that scrolls its own content, which is the only reason the card's height can be constant across nothing-selected, cell-selected and compare mode. Measured three-state proof: ops-matrix-acceptance-smoke.mjs
ACCEPTANCE B, THE MECHANISM: a fact card is a full-width block inside that slot, not a column. Measured narrowest text column on this mount: 835px, against the operator's 560px floor

ACCEPTANCE C, THE MECHANISM: every cell that is not the em-dash Absence carries a bare Anton score and nothing else. Twenty-two of the thirty cells are the dash, eight are scores; the rendered-text enumeration of all thirty is in ops-matrix-acceptance-smoke.mjs

forbid.name: NOTHING EXPANDS IN THE TABLE: no cell spans the table's width
forbid.reason: The operator's first clause. The expanded-row `<td colSpan={regions+1}>` and its `repeat(N,1fr)` per-region fact grid are DELETED, not hidden: a colspan cell reappearing here is the old design coming back.

forbid.name: no fact card is rendered inside the table
forbid.reason: Facts live in the panel below the table, at the card's reading width. A fact inside a region column is what set that column's minimum content width and dragged the table 198px past its container at 1440.

forbid.name: no disclosure glyph on a dimension row
forbid.reason: The row is a selection target now, not a disclosure. A ▸/▾ promises an expansion the table no longer has.

forbid.name: no freshness state word beside a cell score
forbid.reason: The redesigned artboard's cell is a bare number or a bare em dash. The 9.5px uppercase state word under the count ('CURRENT' / 'AGEING') belonged to the design this replaces and doubled the cell's height against the operator's 40px row. RE-STATED 2026-09-09: the operator's delete list names this again, "the words CURRENT and PENDING inside cells and inside fact cards", and requires it measured from RENDERED text with text-transform applied. This runner does exactly that (see run-audit.mjs's `renderedText`, the 2026-09-08 correction), and ops-matrix-acceptance-smoke.mjs enumerates the whole card's rendered text for both words as well.

forbid.name: no 'Compare against:' base-region control
forbid.reason: Superseded, not dropped: the panel's compare mode shows every region's headline figure stacked at reading width, which is what picking a base region and re-reading the columns was trying to achieve. `indexAgainstBase` is still live, inside compare mode.

forbid.name: the literal word UNSCORED as component text
forbid.reason: Operator ruling P1 2.1: the literal token never appears. Absence renders a lowercase fixed-vocabulary word with uppercase CSS, so textContent reads lowercase.

forbid.name: ACCEPTANCE A, THE FORBID: no fact card is rendered OUTSIDE the fixed-height panel slot
forbid.reason: THE TABLE NEVER GROWS (operator 2026-09-09, and coordinator note C3: it is the acceptance test, not a slogan). The card's height is constant because the ONLY box whose content varies with the selection is the panel slot, and that box has a fixed height. Content rendered beside the slot, or back inside the table, is the one way the card can grow again, and it is what this forbids. Proven by attack 2026-09-09: rendering the fact cards as a direct child of the card made this forbid report NOT IN SPEC and the guard's leg A go red with three different heights.

forbid.name: ACCEPTANCE B, THE FORBID: the panel never lays its text out in columns
forbid.reason: The defect he stopped the ship over, in its exact shape: "clicking a dimension row expands five narrow columns of prose under it (Materials sourcing -> 5 columns x N fact cards at ~110px wide)". A `repeat(N, 1fr)` grid inside the panel is that pattern rebuilt one level down, and it is the only way a text box in this panel can fall under the 560px floor while every ancestor stays full width. The measured floor itself is in ops-matrix-acceptance-smoke.mjs leg B.

forbid.name: ACCEPTANCE C, THE FORBID: NO CELL CONTAINS A WORD
forbid.reason: Operator 2026-09-09, third acceptance criterion, verbatim: "no cell contains a word". A cell is either the em-dash Absence part or a bare integer score, so any LETTER in a cell that is not the Absence part is a word coming back. The Absence part is excluded from the selector rather than from the rule because its markup carries a `display:none` word for narrow viewports that `renderedText` would read; its own rendering is enumerated character by character in ops-matrix-acceptance-smoke.mjs leg C, which is where the criterion is actually measured. Proven by attack 2026-09-09: adding the word `sourced` beside a score made this forbid report NOT IN SPEC.
